Alta raises $20M Series A to power AI across fashion
What's the deal? Alta , a styling app founded by Jenny Wang, has raised a $20 million Series A led by Forerunner , which pre-empted the round. Menlo Ventures and Aglaé Ventures Dealroom has a profile for this one. Try Dealroom → , the Arnault family firm behind LVMH , returned as investors. Angels include stylist Meredith Koop, NFL player Paris Johnson Jr., Rylee Martell, and Karlie Kloss Dealroom has a profile for this one. Try Dealroom → .
What's the endgame? Alta builds both a consumer app — modelled on the Clueless closet of mix-and-match outfits — and a B2B service for the fashion industry. It has trained 12 in-house AI models that learn fashion at the item and outfit levels.
Why now? "The fashion industry has been chasing the Clueless closet for 30 years," says Forerunner managing partner Eurie Kim, who is joining Alta's board. "The problem was never a lack of imagination. The technology simply wasn't good enough."
What's the traction? Alta powers AI Outfits and Avatars within Rent the Runway ’s app, and engagement with the tool is running at 35%, ahead of expectations. During the pilot, customers with the outfit experience added to their bag 12% more often than those without it. This feature is now available for all customers.
The fresh capital will fund AI infrastructure, grow Alta's team of 10 across its consumer and enterprise lines, and localise the product across markets. Wang wants Alta to be "the best possible AI provider for this space," with a longer-term vision of AI agents that review users' calendars and travel plans to shop for them.
The signal: At $20 million, Alta's round sits above the 92nd percentile of US fashion Series A deals on record. It reflects a rush of startups — alongside shopping-first rivals Phia and Daydream — racing to pin down AI's best use case in fashion.

Whedon served as an executive producer , along with Tim Minear . The series is set in the year 2517, after the arrival of humans in a new star system, [ 1 ] and follows the adventures of the renegade crew of Serenity , a " Firefly -class" spaceship . The ensemble cast portrays the nine characters living aboard Serenity . Whedon pitched the show as "nine people looking into the blackness of space and seeing nine different things." [ 2 ] The show explores the lives of a group of people, some of whom fought on the losing side of a civil war , making a living on the fringes of society as part of their star system's pioneer culture. The two surviving superpowers, the United States and China, united to form the central federal government, called the Alliance . According to Whedon's vision, "Nothing will change in the future: Technology will advance, but we will still have the same political, moral, and ethical problems as today." [ 3 ] Firefly premiered in the United States on the Fox network on September 20, 2002. By mid-December, it had averaged 4.7 million viewers per episode and was 98th in Nielsen ratings . [ 4 ] It was canceled after 11 of the 14 produced episodes were aired. Despite its short run, it received strong sales when it was released on DVD and has large fan support campaigns. [ 5 ] [ 6 ] It won a Primetime Emmy Award in 2003 for Outstanding Special Visual Effects for a Series . TV Guide ranked it No. 5 on their 2013 list of 60 "shows that were canceled too soon". [ 7 ] [ 8 ] The show's post-airing success led Whedon and Universal Pictures to produce Serenity , a 2005 film that continues the story from the series. [ 5 ] The Firefly franchise expanded into other media, including comics and two tabletop role-playing games . [ 9 ] [ 10 ] On March 15, 2026, star Nathan Fillion confirmed that an animated series was in development with animation by ShadowMachine . Premise [ edit ] Backstory [ edit ] The series takes place in the year 2517, on a variety of planets with numerous habitable moons. The TV series does not reveal whether these celestial bodies are within one star system, only saying that Serenity ' s mode of propulsion through space is a "gravity-drive". Each episode begins with either Book or Captain Reynolds providing the backstory. Book's narration runs as follows: [ 11 ] After the Earth was used up, we found a new solar system, and hundreds of new Earths were terraformed and colonized. The central planets formed the Alliance and decided all the planets had to join under their rule. There was some disagreement on that point. After the war, many of the Independents who had fought and lost drifted to the edges of the system, far from Alliance control. Out here, people struggle to get by with the most basic technologies. A ship would bring you work. A gun would help you keep it. A captain's goal was simple: Find a crew. Find a job. Keep flying. —   Derrial Book, introductory narrative for the show The film Serenity reveals that the planets and moons are in an extensive system, and production documents related to the film indicate that there is no faster-than-light travel in this universe . The outlying settlements often did not receive support in the construction of their civilizations. This resulted in many border planets and moons having forbidding, dry environments, well-suited to the Western genre. Preference Model Raises $16 Million Seed Round Led By Andreessen Horowitz
Preference Model raised $16 million in seed funding led by Andreessen Horowitz, with participation from SignalFire, South Park Commons, Scale Angel Group, and researchers including Fei-Fei Li, Ian Goodfellow, and Julian Schrittwieser. Pasted text
The company focuses on building reinforcement learning environments to train more capable, better-aligned AI systems.
Preference Model said it has spent the past year developing RL environments for several frontier AI laboratories.
The company’s work centers on creating training environments that resist reward hacking, where AI models exploit weaknesses in a task or grading system instead of solving the intended problem.
Its technology helps AI labs build harder, more reliable environments as models become increasingly capable of identifying shortcuts and vulnerabilities.
Alongside the funding, Preference Model open-sourced Karotte, a framework it has used internally to develop RL environments.
Karotte has undergone more than one million evaluation runs and controlled red-teaming exercises. Pasted text
The framework provides secure defaults and tools intended to prevent agents from manipulating graders, accessing unintended information, exhausting system resources, or otherwise exploiting training infrastructure.
Preference Model views robust training environments as an increasingly important part of AI alignment, particularly because reward-hacking behavior discovered during training can become reinforced rather than merely producing inaccurate benchmark results.
Andreessen Horowitz said Preference Model is focused on an area increasingly important to AI labs: building the infrastructure needed to identify model weaknesses, generate more challenging tasks, and test environments against agents actively attempting to break them. Pasted text
The financing will support Preference Model as it continues developing reinforcement learning infrastructure and tools intended for frontier AI developers.

Luxor Technology Raises $16 Million Strategic Round Led By CMT Digital
By Amit Chowdhry

Luxor Technology Raises $16 Million Strategic Round Led By CMT Digital
Luxor Technology has raised $16 million in strategic financing led by CMT Digital to expand its AI compute, hardware, energy, and derivatives businesses. Canaan, MicroBT, Halo, Steelhead, and additional angel investors participated in the round, which includes a combination of primary and secondary capital.
Luxor said it selected its investors partly for their operational involvement across the compute supply chain, including hardware, energy, capital, and financial markets.
The fundraising follows the September launch of Luxor AI, which extends infrastructure and market expertise originally developed for Bitcoin mining into AI and high-performance computing.
Luxor’s hardware brokerage operation has traded approximately $1 billion of ASIC mining equipment. Its energy business services more than 75 MW of electrical load across the ERCOT and Southwest Power Pool markets, while the company’s agentic cloud platform had processed 1.8 million workloads year-to-date as of September.
Luxor plans to use the new capital to scale its agentic cloud platform, provide working capital for its expanding AI hardware business, grow compute derivatives trading and market-making capabilities, and hire additional engineering and go-to-market employees.
The company’s AI hardware operation sources GPUs and AI servers through a network of partners and also participates in special allocations, abandoned orders, and used equipment markets.
Luxor is additionally developing financial products around AI compute.
Its over-the-counter operation provides cash-settled options, forwards, and backstops based on compute-rental indexes, applying concepts from financial derivatives markets to computing capacity.
CMT Digital brings experience in electronic trading, market structure, and technology development as Luxor seeks to turn AI compute into a more standardized and tradable market.
Luxor’s broader platform spans hardware, software, finance, energy, compute trading, and data infrastructure across both Bitcoin mining and AI.

Bitcoin Mining Firm Luxor Raises $16 Million to Accelerate AI Expansion Published: Oct 27, 2026, 6:45 PM EDT
BTC $74,825 ( -1.15% )

Bitcoin Mining Firm Luxor Raises $16 Million to Accelerate AI Expansion
Bitcoin mining technology company Luxor has raised $16 million in a strategic funding round led by CMT Digital, accelerating its expansion into artificial intelligence infrastructure as cryptocurrency mining businesses increasingly pursue opportunities in the rapidly growing AI computing market.
WRITTEN BY
Andrew Hayward
SHARE Published: Oct 27, 2026, 6:45 PM EDT
Key Takeaways
Luxor raised $16 million in a funding round led by CMT Digital to accelerate its expansion into AI computing, hardware trading, and financial derivatives.
Bitcoin miners are increasingly pivoting to AI, with companies including Hut 8, Terawulf, Core Scientific, IREN, and Cipher investing heavily in AI infrastructure.
Luxor is taking a different approach, focusing on supplying hardware, software, and financial services to the AI industry rather than converting mining facilities into data centers.
Luxor Raises $16 Million
The Seattle-based company announced the investment Tuesday, with participation from bitcoin mining hardware manufacturers Canaan and MicroBT, along with Halo, Steelhead, and several angel investors. The financing includes both primary and secondary capital, although Luxor did not disclose the breakdown or its valuation.
The funding follows Luxor’s September launch of Luxor AI, a business division designed to bring the company’s existing expertise in energy management, computing hardware, financial derivatives, and software into the AI and high-performance computing (HPC) sectors.
Luxor said it will use the capital to expand its AI-focused cloud platform, provide working capital for its growing hardware trading business, increase its activity in computing derivatives and market-making, and hire additional engineering and business development personnel.
The company is building on its established bitcoin mining operations, which include a mining pool, specialized hardware brokerage, firmware, energy services, and financial products that allow miners to hedge fluctuations in computing revenue.
According to Luxor, its hardware brokerage has facilitated $1 billion in bitcoin mining equipment transactions, while its energy division manages more than 75 megawatts of electrical load across the ERCOT and Southwest Power Pool markets. Its AI cloud platform had processed 1.8 million workloads year-to-date as of September.
Luxor is also expanding its brokerage of graphics processing units and AI servers, tapping relationships with equipment manufacturers and suppliers to source hardware in an increasingly competitive market.
Another focus is the development of financial derivatives tied to computing capacity. Luxor already offers over-the-counter options, forwards, and other contracts linked to computing rental indexes, extending a model it previously developed for Bitcoin mining hashrate.
“Compute markets are converging: the same miners, power sites and capital that served digital mining are now powering AI,” Luxor CEO and co-founder Nick Hansen said in the announcement.
Bitcoin Miners Shift Focus to AI
The investment comes as bitcoin mining companies increasingly redirect their infrastructure and capital toward AI, seeking revenue opportunities beyond the volatile economics of cryptocurrency production.
In July, Bitcoin.com News reported that Hut 8 had secured a $9.8 billion, 15-year lease for an additional 352 megawatts of AI computing capacity at its Beacon Point campus in Texas. The agreement doubled the tenant’s commitment at the site to 704 megawatts.
Meanwhile, Terawulf has undertaken an aggressive expansion into AI infrastructure. In May, the company acquired a Kentucky data center site targeting one gigawatt of high-performance computing capacity by 2030, with its AI revenue already surpassing bitcoin mining revenue during the first quarter of 2026.
Other major mining companies, including Core Scientific, IREN, and Cipher, have similarly repurposed or reduced bitcoin mining operations to accommodate AI computing customers.
The transition has not been without costs. An October analysis published by Bitcoin.com News estimated that publicly traded miners shed approximately 75 exahash per second of realized bitcoin mining capacity during the first half of 2026, representing roughly $1.5 billion in equivalent hardware investment.
Unlike operators converting large mining facilities into AI data centers, Luxor is positioning itself as a provider of the hardware, software, trading, and financial infrastructure serving both industries.

Home / Companies / Start Ups / Cent raises $15 million to expand AI-powered preventive healthcare platform
Cent raises $15 million to expand AI-powered preventive healthcare platform
Blume Ventures and South Park Commons led the funding round as Cent plans to expand its AI-powered medical imaging, diagnostics and preventive healthcare services in India
(L–R): Anshul Khandelwal, Co-founder, Cent; Shashank ND, Founder, Practo and OneFlow Holdings; and Arpit Garg, Co-founder, Cent. Peerzada Abrar Bengaluru
4 min read Last Updated : Oct 27 2026 | 5:06 PM IST
Listen to This Article
Cent, a preventive health intelligence company, has raised $15 million in its Series A round, comprising equity and debt, led by Blume Ventures and existing investor South Park Commons. The round also saw participation from individual investors such as Arun Sarin, former CEO of Vodafone; Srinivas Narayanan, former CTO (B2B) of OpenAI; Sharath Narayana, Krishna Sridhar and Aprameya Radhakrishna.
Cent was founded in 2025 by Shashank ND, founder of Practo and OneFlow Holdings; Anshul Khandelwal, former chief marketing officer of Ola Electric; and Arpit Garg, former product head at Lenskart.
“When we were introduced to Shashank and the team that came together to build Cent, we saw an obsessive ambition to solve for accurate diagnosis and protocols for cancers amongst other indications,” said Karthik Reddy, co-founder and managing partner, Blume Ventures. “We are believers in Cent’s vision to extend this from India to the world over time and it is in line with our conviction around health tech for a decade now.”
They started it because, in India, heart disease, cancer and metabolic diseases are usually detected only after symptoms appear, when they are much harder to treat. Cent exists to close that gap, so serious illnesses are detected while they can still be treated simply or prevented altogether. Cent is building a vertically integrated preventive health platform that combines purpose-built hardware, AI-driven radiology and diagnostics, and bioinformatics. Together, these allow Cent to detect diseases years before symptoms appear and to track each member's health over time, building towards a future where healthcare is preventive, continuous and personalised. The funding will go into this R&D and into expanding Cent's AI, engineering and clinical teams.
“With every scan, Cent has shown that early detection changes lives. Behind every one of those scans is a family that otherwise wouldn’t have known what was wrong,” said Prateek Mehta, general partner, South Park Commons India. “They’re the right people to build this, committed to the belief that no one should find out about a tumour or a blocked artery when it’s too late.”

Cent has also acquired the Medsee platform, founded by Chitra Singh, an AI-powered radiology reporting workflow built for qualified medical professionals. The platform drafts structured reports and highlights findings for radiologist review, enabling Cent to deliver faster, more consistent reporting as scan volumes grow.
“India's healthcare system is still built to treat illness, not to find it early. We believe the next shift is preventive care that is precise and accessible at scale. Our first 10,000 scans have shown us how much that shift is needed,” said Anshul Khandelwal, co-founder, Cent. “This investment lets us go deeper into AI, medical imaging and clinical research, and build preventive health infrastructure in India that can serve the world.”
Today, members experience Cent through Cent Check, its flagship full-body health check. In a single visit of about two hours, they undergo full-body MRI, low-dose CT, DEXA, ECG, ECHO and tests for over 100 biomarkers under Cent's proprietary protocol. Cent's AI brings every result into one picture of the body, specialist doctors review each finding, and members leave with a doctor-led plan and support throughout the year.
The firm said that among members who felt well when they came in, one in four had a finding worth acting on, and one in 40 needed immediate medical attention, including early-stage tumours, significantly narrowed arteries and aneurysms. Every scan also adds to one of the largest datasets on the health of asymptomatic Indians. Cent will use it to build Indian baselines for a healthy body, train models that flag disease risk earlier, and support clinical research, so preventive care keeps getting more precise as Cent grows.

candidates.text:
Nearhuman raises £350,000 pre-seed to bring physical AI to e-scooters
PRESS RELEASE GlobeNewswire
Oct. 6, 2026, 08:30 AM
BRISTOL, United Kingdom, Oct. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Nearhuman, a physical AI start-up based at Bristol Robotics Laboratory, has raised £350,000 in pre-seed funding led by SFC Capital. The funding will support the development of on-device safety technology for shared e-scooter and e-bike fleets.
Shared e-scooters have become part of everyday travel in many cities, and the number of people hurt has grown with them. E-scooter casualties in Great Britain have more than tripled since official records began, from 454 in 2020 to 1,477 in 2025, according to Department for Transport figures. Europe is seeing a similar trend: in Germany, police recorded 16,496 e-scooter accidents with injuries in 2025, up 38% in a year, while e-scooter deaths in France almost doubled, from 45 to 80.
Operators, councils and road safety groups are working on the problem through better infrastructure, rider education, enforcement and vehicle design. One gap that remains is data: there is often limited direct evidence of how and where vehicles are actually ridden.
Nearhuman is developing a camera module that fits onto vehicles already on the street. AI running on the vehicle is designed to detect pavement riding, close calls with pedestrians and road hazards as they happen. Footage is processed and redacted on board, so sensitive video does not need to leave the vehicle.
The aim is to give operators safety insights without replacing their fleets, and in time to give councils street-level information on the condition of roads, cycle lanes and pavements, gathered by vehicles already travelling across the city.
Founder Faizan Mir grew up in Kashmir and was building things from an early age. At 14, he built a drone and a working flamethrower, earning national recognition. His father's response stayed with him: "How does a flamethrower help people? Build something that makes the world a better place."
Mir took the advice. At 16, he represented North India in Mobile Robotics at IndiaSkills, the national skills competition, and won a Medallion for Excellence. He went on to study robotics at UWE Bristol before founding Nearhuman.
"My father's question has shaped everything I've built since," said Mir, 24, Nearhuman's chief executive. "Shared scooters and bikes are one of the best things to happen to cities, but the people responsible for them often lack good data on what happens on the street. Technology on its own won't fix that. Better streets, education and enforcement all matter. What we can do is help give operators and councils clearer evidence, with privacy built into the hardware. I think my father would approve of this one."
"AI has changed how we work on screens. The next shift is AI that runs inside physical machines, and Nearhuman is building for exactly that," said Ed Stevenson, Principal at SFC Capital. "E-scooters are a smart place to start, a real safety problem in UK cities today. But what Nearhuman is really building is the intelligence layer for the physical world."
Nearhuman's live pilot in Bristol will test the system in real-world conditions, and the company plans to release further AI products in the coming months. The funding will support product development, on-street testing and commercial deployment.
ENDS
Notes to editors
About Nearhuman
Nearhuman is a Bristol-based AI company building intelligence for the physical world. Combining computer vision, on-device AI and integrated hardware, it develops technology that helps vehicles and machines understand their surroundings. Its first commercial application brings real-time safety detection to shared e-scooter and e-bike fleets, through retrofit systems designed to identify unsafe riding and road hazards. Nearhuman's approach is built around key challenges in deploying physical AI: protecting privacy, working with limited computing power and reducing reliance on continuous cloud connectivity. Founded by Faizan Mir, backed by SFC Capital and based at Bristol Robotics Laboratory, the company is developing a broader portfolio of physical AI technologies. nearhuman.co/?utm_source=globenewswire
About SFC Capital
SFC Capital is the UK's most active seed-stage investor, providing seed capital and support to promising British startups. By combining our leading investment funds with our angel syndicate, we have created a unique model that provides investors with diversified exposure to high-potential SEIS and EIS-qualifying businesses. Since 2012, SFC has invested in over 650 startups and partnered with the likes of British Business Investments to support innovation across all UK regions. To learn more about what we do and see our portfolio, visit sfccapital.com.

AI startup Visorway raises pre-seed funding
Financing

08.10.2026
Zurich-based Startup Visorway, the AI-native service firm for sourcing and procurement, has closed its pre-seed financing round. The investment will be used to expand the services customers run on Visorway and to grow the network of domain experts behind them.
A large share of organisations’ spending goes towards services such as consultants, implementers and external teams. In its March 2026 essay “Services: The New Software”, Sequoia Capital estimates that companies spend roughly six dollars on services for every dollar spent on software. It however predicts that companies will often replace traditional human service providers with AI-native service provider – AI-autopilot – that deliver the completed outcome.
Founded in 2026, Visorway is already operating as an AI autopilot for IT sourcing for corporate procurement teams and sourcing advisory firms. As an AI-native service firm, it encodes the methodology of leading practitioners– for tasks such as scoping, drafting and evaluating a tender –and delivers the resulting work directly through AI, with experienced practitioners validating the output.
“AI should structure work, not replace thinking,” said Jan Appenzeller, CEO and Co-Founder of Visorway. “We encode how experienced practitioners actually work, deliver that work through AI, and have those same practitioners validate what comes out. The expertise is not in the model. It is in the method.”
Visorway’s first services cover IT tender documentation for both private and public procurement, built on methodology from advisors with decades of Swiss sourcing and public procurement experience. Proof-of-value engagements are running with Swiss enterprises, a federal research institution, and sourcing advisory firms using Visorway in client delivery.
With the obtained funding, the company says it plans to extend its AI-native service model beyond sourcing into other professional domains, combining practitioner methodologies with AI-based delivery and expert validation. Backed entirely by angel investors, the company is now valued at CHF 3 million. Several of the individual investors in the round have operating backgrounds in the industries Visorway serves.

Unveilr AI raises pre-seed round from AJVC at Rs 16.7 Cr valuation
Mumbai based Unveilr AI has raised an undisclosed amount in a pre-seed round from Aviral Bhatnagar’s AJVC at a valuation of Rs 16.7 crore.
Shashank Pathak
01 Oct 2026
11:30
IST
Follow Us
New Update
Mumbai based Unveilr AI has raised an undisclosed amount in a pre-seed round from Aviral Bhatnagar’s AJVC at a valuation of Rs 16.7 crore.
The startup will use the fresh capital to expand its engineering team and develop additional capabilities for its AI agents. It also plans to grow its sales team and expand its customer base across India, the UAE and the US.
Founded by Sanditya Srivastava, the startup helps B2B and consumer brands generate leads through Google and AI search platforms such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Claude.
Unveilr AI combines search engine optimisation (SEO) with Answer Engine Optimisation (AEO). Its AI agents track how brands appear across search engines, identify queries where competitors are recommended and analyse the sources used by AI platforms. Its team then works on content, technical changes and online authority to improve brand visibility.
The startup claims that its customers can start seeing results within the first month. For an Indian B2B legal services platform, Unveilr AI increased AI sourced traffic by around 4.7 times and leads by 5 times, along with an 80% increase in ChatGPT citations. For a D2C brand, organic search contributes around 27% of total revenue.
Launched in February 2026, Unveilr AI currently serves B2B and consumer brands across India, the UAE and the US. The company has a team comprising IIT alumni and SEO and AEO specialists.

candidates.snippet: GUDEA raises $7 mn in seed funding for AI narrative intelligence Beinsure
candidates.text:
InsurTech News
🇺🇸 US Insurance News
GUDEA raised $7 mn in an oversubscribed seed funding round co-led by Mudita Ventures and Collide Capital to accelerate product development and enterprise expansion.
The AI-powered platform uses behavioral intelligence, graph neural networks and real-time monitoring to identify how online narratives originate, spread and influence markets.
GUDEA serves Fortune 100 companies and communications firms, with its technology designed to distinguish authentic engagement from coordinated or inauthentic online activity.
AI-powered narrative intelligence company GUDEA has raised $7 mn in an oversubscribed seed financing round co-led by Mudita Ventures and Collide Capital. The investment will support product development, broader monitoring coverage and expansion of its enterprise business.
GUDEA, which describes its platform as a “Storm Tracker for the Internet,” develops technology that helps organizations identify the origins, participants and potential impact of narratives circulating across digital platforms.
The company targets a growing challenge for businesses and financial markets: online discussions can develop into influential narratives within hours, often before organizations understand who initiated them or how they gained momentum.
According to GUDEA’s internal research, relatively small groups of users displaying inauthentic behavior can account for a disproportionate share of online discussions involving consumer brands, financial markets and other topics.
Such activity can complicate how communications teams, corporate strategists and investor relations professionals assess emerging reputational and business risks.
GUDEA’s platform combines behavioral analysis, graph neural network modeling and real-time monitoring across dozens of online services. Its technology tracks where narratives originate, identifies influential participants and estimates how quickly information may spread.
The system also distinguishes authentic engagement from potentially inauthentic activity and classifies audiences into five categories, providing organizations with information intended to support earlier identification of emerging risks.
GUDEA says its research has contributed to reporting by national news organizations, while its technology is used by Fortune 100 companies and major communications firms. The company was also selected as a finalist for the 2026 SXSW Pitch competition and nominated for a 2026 Webby Award.
“Every organization now operates inside an information environment it does not control and often cannot see,” said Keith Presley, GUDEA’s co-founder and CEO.
Narratives shape markets, brands, and public trust long before they show up in a headline. The demand behind this round reflects a simple reality: leaders need to know what is moving online, who is moving it, and what happens next. We are scaling the platform and the team to give them exactly that.
Keith Presley, GUDEA’s co-founder and CEO
The funding comes as GUDEA seeks to expand the application of narrative intelligence beyond conventional social media monitoring, with an emphasis on behavioral patterns and the networks responsible for distributing information.
Buddy Foster, an investor at Mudita Ventures, said the firm’s decision to participate reflected its assessment of GUDEA’s technology and existing enterprise relationships.
The information environment has become a core business risk, and GUDEA measures it with a rigor we have not seen anywhere else in the market. Keith and his team pair deep intelligence experience with technology that already delivers for demanding clients, and we are proud to back them as they scale
Buddy Foster, an investor at Mudita Ventures
The new capital will allow GUDEA to increase its platform’s monitoring capabilities and support enterprise adoption as organizations seek more detailed information about the development and distribution of online narratives.
Peter Sonner

He covers InsurTech and FinTech, startup funding, artificial intelligence, blockchain, cryptoassets, and digital transformation in insurance. Founded in 2026 by Sarat Addanki, Michael (Mick) Gallagher and Anuraag Nallapati, Shamrock AI is headquartered in Shillong, Meghalaya, with offices in Hyderabad and San Francisco. Shamrock AI has raised $5 million in a seed funding round led by Endiya Partners , with participation from Capria Ventures .
The company's first institutional funding round will support product development, team expansion and go-to-market efforts.
Founded in 2026 by Sarat Addanki, Michael (Mick) Gallagher and Anuraag Nallapati, Shamrock AI is headquartered in Shillong, Meghalaya, with offices in Hyderabad and San Francisco. The company serves multiple Fortune 500 customers, including a Fortune 100 AI hardware manufacturer and a Fortune 100 healthcare company.
“It is rare to see an early-stage startup with such technical and domain expertise alongside deep enterprise trust from Fortune 500 companies,” said Anvesh Ramineni, partner at Endiya Partners.
The startup is building an enterprise business knowledge graph that connects business processes, systems, data and configurations, giving AI agents the context required to operate reliably across critical workflows.
“Enterprises are looking to move beyond AI experimentation and deploy agents across critical business processes, but doing so reliably requires a deep understanding of how their businesses operate,” said Nallapati.
Its initial focus is agentic test lifecycle automation for enterprise resource planning (ERP) transformations, including SAP S/4HANA migrations. The platform continuously tests and validates business processes, building a representation of how an enterprise operates that can subsequently support data observability and autonomous business process automation.
The company plans to expand its workforce across India and the US, with 70-80 per cent of employees expected to be based in India and a client-facing team in the US. It also plans to expand its presence in the Middle East.
“With some of the world’s largest technology and healthcare companies already among its customers, Shamrock exemplifies what we look for at Capria: deep domain expertise, measurable enterprise value, and the ability to build globally competitive AI businesses from India,” said Surya Mantha, managing partner at Capria Ventures.

Space robotics startup Cosmochute raises $1.5 Mn in pre-seed round
Founded this year by Janhavi Gore, Amit Chowdhary and Dhruv Alok Sangal, Cosmochute is building space robotics infrastructure for the emerging lunar economy.
Gyan Vardhan
15 Oct 2026
11:01
IST
Follow Us
New Update
Space robotics startup Cosmochute has raised $1.5 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Accel and Prosus Ventures under the Atoms X programme. IIMA Ventures’ Deep-tech and Aerospace Acceleration Fund, Operators Studio and Chinmayi Muthyala also participated in the round.
Cosmochute is among seven startups selected for the inaugural Atoms X cohort, which was launched earlier this year.
The company will use the proceeds for product development, engineering team expansion and its commercial roadmap, as it prepares for its next phase of growth, Cosmochute said in a press release.
Founded this year by Janhavi Gore, Amit Chowdhary and Dhruv Alok Sangal, Cosmochute is building space robotics infrastructure for the emerging lunar economy. Its first programme, LEAP, is a modular platform designed to support payload transportation and deployment on the Moon.
LEAP combines a modular rover and trailer with standard payload bays, allowing multiple payloads to be integrated into a common mission architecture. The company aims to address the cost and complexity of delivering equipment and payloads to the lunar surface through a standardised approach to lunar transportation and deployment.
The platform is designed to reduce the need for mission specific engineering and make lunar transportation and payload deployment more repeatable.
Cosmochute is setting up its lunar laboratories at IIMA Ventures’ incubation facility. The startup is also working within India’s space technology ecosystem, which includes companies, investors and institutions supporting private participation in the sector.
With LEAP as its first platform, Cosmochute plans to develop capabilities in lunar mobility and space robotics, with potential applications in other in space and terrestrial use cases. The company aims to build infrastructure to support commercial and scientific missions to the Moon.

candidates.snippet: PropertyGuru ex-CEO’s AI Health Startup Genie Health Raises Seed Funding https://www.tabla.com.sg/
candidates.text:
Community
PropertyGuru ex-CEO’s AI Health Startup Genie Health Raises Seed Funding
PUBLISHED Oct 22, 2026, 3:51 PM
Hari Krishnan, co-founder and CEO of Genie Health. PHOTO: GENIE HEALTH
PHOTO: GENIE HEALTH
An annual health checkup when Mr Hari Krishnan was still CEO of PropertyGuru led him to to start Genie Health, an artificial intelligence healthtech startup.
He was found to have high cholesterol, after which he drew on his family’s medical history, data from wearable devices and advice from medical professionals for a better understanding of his health.
But he recognised that the resources and expertise he had access to as a CEO might not be readily available to everyone.
“The more I thought about it, I saw that this was not something that had to do with power or authority,” he said. “This information needs to be democratised and made more available, and that’s where Genie comes in.”
Mr Hari, the startup’s CEO and co-founder, has now raised US$3 million (S$3.83 million) in seed funding to develop tools to improve consumers’ understanding of their health information, and enable healthcare providers to deliver more personalised care.
The funding round was led by the Nadathur Family Office, the family office of Infosys Technologies co-founder Mr NS Raghavan. Other investors include Temasek-backed venture studio Liminal and undisclosed angel investors who are senior leaders in the healthcare space, said Mr Hari.
Mr Anand Nadathur, principal of the Nadathur Family Office, will join the board.
Mr Hari and his co-founders – Genie’s chairperson, Ms Maya Hari, and the startup’s chief marketing officer, Mr Sandeep Suvarna – also took part in the funding round and collectively maintain the largest bloc of shares.
Ms Maya, who used to be CEO at climate-tech platform Terrascope, backed by Olam and Fujitsu Ventures, also had a stint as vice-president for the Asia-Pacific at Twitter.
Mr Sandeep was the former head of international marketing at live-streaming platform Twitch.
Using AI to personalise healthcare
Genie Health has two products: a free app for patients to get insights and guidance on their health information, and a platform for healthcare providers to engage and provide insights to patients.
The platform for healthcare providers charges a monthly subscription and some usage-based fees.
It uses AI agents to automate routine administrative tasks. One such tool is a triaging agent which handles customer enquiries and can refer medical questions to a human during office hours, or direct customers to a hospital outside office hours.
“We are seeing up to 60 per cent fewer enquiries handled by (our) human staff,” said Mr Hari.
Another AI agent that handles appointment bookings and sends reminders to patients has reduced no-shows at clinics by 25 per cent.
Navigating a regulated space
Building a startup in a heavily regulated space such as healthcare is not easy, but Mr Hari believes that the co-founders’ years of experience and complementary skill sets give them an edge.
“As a repeat entrepreneur, I know exactly what is important to focus on and what you can tolerate,” he added.
The key to success lies in finding partners, and this is not something that may occur to young entrepreneurs looking to disrupt their industry, said Krishnan.
Before starting up Genie, the founders had conversations with healthcare providers and sought partners for the venture. They have a list of advisers, which includes four medical doctors – resource persons who field questions from Mr Hari and his team on how things work in the medical field and what the challenges are.
“(The healthcare industry) needs to be regulated for logical reasons, but to be honest, there is enough space left for innovation,” said Mr Hari.
Both of Genie’s products are unregulated because they are not direct healthcare service providers, but Mr Hari said they comply with the Personal Data Protection Act and US’ Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act.
Singapore first, expansion later
Genie will be focused on Singapore for the next 12 months, as the startup is looking for good unit economics and product-market fit here.
The funding will be used to deepen Genie’s presence in Singapore, to build more integration with the healthcare system, and to get more clinics on board the platform.
Other features are slated to be rolled out, and Mr Hari is looking to educate members of the public and healthcare providers about how its AI tools can be used.
“Once we have hit those parameters, we will explore other markets, but we don’t want to get distracted by that; our focus is very much here in Singapore,” he said.
Genie is also looking to maintain a lean team with its AI focus. It now has 10 employees, including the three co-founders, and will use AI to keep the headcount below 20.
This will require a reimagination of how business is done and how the company can scale, said Mr Hari.
“How do you do this by using AI and technology? This is going to require us to think about it.” THE BUSINESS TIMES

Still, the story has a detail that larger rounds rarely offer: the lead investor was the startup’s first paid business customer before it wrote a cheque. That sequence says more about product-market fit than most pitch decks do.
The money will go toward expanding INVE’s business platform and growing its consumer product beyond weddings. The business platform only launched in August 2026, so the company is funding a product that launched in August 2026 and is still being introduced to more companies. This analysis walks through what is confirmed, what the platform does, why the engineering behind a digital invitation is harder than it looks, and where the open questions sit.

INVE’s $300K Pre-Seed at a Glance
Every figure below comes from the announcement coverage. Nothing in the table is estimated, and anything the reports did not state is left out. That gap matters, because pre-seed announcements often leave out the terms people most want to know.
Item Reported detail
Company INVE, Saudi-based event-tech
Round Pre-seed
Amount US$300,000
Lead investor Outliers Venture Capital
Founded 2024, by Abdulrahman Alabdulkarim
Consumer reach 250 events across more than 60 cities and towns in Saudi Arabia and the GCC
Business platform launch August 2026
Stated use of funds Expand the business platform, grow the consumer product beyond weddings
Immediate priority markets Saudi Arabia and the GCC
Two numbers stand out. The 250 events across 60-plus locations average out to about four events per city or town if they were spread evenly, though real usage almost certainly clusters in a handful of large cities. The second number is the two-year gap between founding in 2024 and the business launch in August 2026. INVE spent most of its life as a consumer product and only recently added a second revenue line. The consumer side also sent more than 35,000 invitations and recorded an 88% RSVP response rate, which suggests guests do engage with the invitations once they arrive.

Who Is Behind INVE and Outliers VC
The announcement names one founder, Abdulrahman Alabdulkarim, and one investor, Outliers Venture Capital. The reports do not name any other founders, executives or co-investors, so this article does not either. If a syndicate joined the round, the coverage did not say so.
Outliers plays two roles in this story, and the overlap is the interesting part. It was INVE’s first paid business-design partner, and it then invested. A fund that pays for a product before backing it has seen the software in daily use, hit its rough edges and decided to stay anyway. Diligence rarely gets closer to the product than that.
The relationship also carries a caveat. A customer-investor has an obvious incentive to talk up the product it uses. Readers should treat the Outliers endorsement as a strong signal of real usage, not as independent proof that the platform will scale to customers who have no stake in INVE’s success. The next few paying customers who are not investors will tell the real story.
From Wedding Invitations to a Business Platform
INVE started with consumers. Its personalised invitations have supported 250 events across more than 60 cities and towns in Saudi Arabia and the GCC, and the funding is meant to push the consumer product beyond weddings. Weddings are a sensible starting wedge for an invitation product. They involve a fixed guest list, a hard date, strong emotional stakes and a host willing to pay for polish.
They are also a trap. A wedding happens once for most customers, which makes repeat usage hard to build. Moving into other occasions gives the consumer product more reasons to return, and the reports confirm that widening is the stated plan. The announcement did not list the new event types, so this article does not guess at them.

What's the endgame? Deload consolidates training-plan generation, workout management, client check-ins, and payments into one platform. Its AI drafts programs spanning 12 to 16 weeks, which the trainer reviews, approves, and customizes — the trainer remains the "coach of record."
How it works. The workflow begins with a trainer's approach and a client's intake information. "Your approach. Their intake. Deload drafts the plan. You approve it," the company says. Trainers can then edit sessions in plain English, with downstream weeks adjusting automatically.
Why now? Both founders, Sean Frasure and Ethan Rasmussen, came through Utah Valley University's Sandbox entrepreneurship program and the Startup Ignition Bootcamp. The company — rebranded from Revyl — placed third at UVU's ZinnStarter pitch competition in April 2026.

Hyderabad-based Physical AI startup Tensrai has raised Rs 3.4 crore in a pre-seed funding from India Accelerator, Finvolve, Hyderabad Angels and other angels.
The fresh capital will be used to accelerate technology development, strengthen

New Update
Hyderabad-based Physical AI startup Tensrai has raised Rs 3.4 crore in a pre-seed funding from India Accelerator, Finvolve, Hyderabad Angels and other angels.
The fresh capital will be used to accelerate technology development, strengthen engineering and deployment capabilities, and support expansion into domestic and international markets, Tensrai said in a press release.
Co-founded by Sai Nikhil Rao Gona, Venkata Sai Charan Chalamalasetty, Harshith Uppalapati, and Vivek Datta, Tensrai is developing a unified, retrofittable autonomy platform that enables industrial and commercial robots, vehicles and machines to perform physical tasks autonomously.
The platform combines vision-first navigation, AI-based localisation, vision-language model (VLM)-powered reasoning, autonomous mobility, robotic arm manipulation and vision-language-action (VLA)-based teach-and-deploy capabilities. The technology is designed to help machines perceive their surroundings, reason through tasks, learn skills and execute operations with limited human intervention.
Tensrai aims to bring autonomous capabilities to both purpose-built machines and existing equipment through retrofitting, potentially reducing the cost and complexity of adopting robotics across industrial and commercial settings.
The startup is targeting applications such as autonomous material handling and cleaning across factories, warehouses, airports, hospitals, shopping malls and commercial campuses. It is also developing a general-purpose mobile manipulator that combines autonomous mobility with robotic arms to perform tasks across material handling, cleaning, manufacturing and construction.
Tensrai plans to generate revenue through multiple streams, including robot sales, autonomy retrofitting, Robot-as-a-Service (RaaS) and customised solutions. It also plans to expand into international markets.
The funding comes amid growing interest in Physical AI, which combines artificial intelligence with robotic systems and machines to enable them to understand and interact with the physical world. Unlike software-based AI applications, Physical AI systems are designed to translate perception and reasoning into real-world actions.
With a common autonomy platform for different types of machines, Tensrai aims to help businesses automate repetitive, labour-intensive and operationally complex tasks across industrial and commercial settings.

QwikBuild, an enterprise AI startup that builds bespoke software and AI agents for business operations, has raised $2.3 million in pre-seed funding. The startup is backed by Globalway Inc., Blume Ventures, Marsshot, and DeVC, alongside prominent angel investors including Lalit Keshre (founder of Groww) and Ankit Nagori (founder of Cure.fit).
Alongside the raise, QwikBuild announced a joint venture with Globalway Inc, a publicly listed Japanese company, to drive its expansion into Japan’s enterprise market.
Launched last year by Pradeep Ayyagari, QwikBuild is an enterprise AI platform that lets businesses build bespoke, enterprise-grade software & AI agents in days rather than months. Using AI agents, it turns manual operations into production-ready applications that organisations own and control.
The Bengaluru-based startup addresses the gap of manual processes by using autonomous AI agents; it builds bespoke, enterprise-grade software in days rather than months. The platform meets businesses exactly where they are through three paths: replacing a legacy system entirely, building a custom layer on top of existing tools like SAP and Salesforce, or building from scratch
Built to work alongside existing enterprise systems, including SAP. QwikBuild helps businesses modernise workflows, streamline and unlock the AI agent era for their operations. It said that its platform is already in use by enterprises across the US, Singapore, India, with clients like Asia’s largest electronics component exporter that now runs its shipment and supply-chain on software and AI agents.
Through this combination of AI-driven development, enterprise integrations and Managed agents stack, QwikBuild aims to help businesses in their AI transformation journey by modernising their operations around their core systems, without the time and complexity of traditional custom software projects.

candidates.text:
5 min

Live2.ai, an artificial intelligence startup that helps brands analyse social media activity and manage marketing campaigns, has raised ₹130 crore in a pre-Series B funding round led by IvyCap Ventures, according to an announcement on October 27.
The round includes primary capital for business expansion and a secondary component that provides partial liquidity to early shareholders.
Live2.ai said that it will use the fresh capital to develop its AI agent platform, expand its enterprise business and strengthen its cloud infrastructure across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific. It also plans to expand its engineering, data science and customer success teams across North America, Europe, Singapore and India, the company said.
Live2.ai operates under Woovly India Private Limited, according to its privacy policy. The business was previously part of Woovly, which Xelpmoc Design and Tech included in its portfolio. In a June 2025 earnings call, Xelpmoc described Live2.ai as Woovly’s software-as-a-service (SaaS) business, focused on interactive shoppable videos and live commerce.
The company also offers a shoppable video product through the Shopify App Store. The app allows businesses to add interactive videos to online stores , with features for product discovery, customer engagement and analytics. Its Shopify listing provides public pricing for subscription plans, including an enterprise tier.
Live2.ai’s broader platform monitors brand conversations across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, X and review websites. The company says its software helps brands identify consumer trends, plan and publish social media content, track campaign performance and audit influencer and user-generated content.
The startup also offers tools to turn content cleared for commercial use into shoppable experiences. It said its platform uses eight AI agents for tasks such as crisis detection, trend identification, campaign auditing and automated responses, with governance controls and human review.
Live2.ai said it serves more than 200 brands across the United States, Europe and Southeast Asia. Its reported customers include Henkel’s Schwarzkopf, Salonory, Titan Brands and Shiseido.
The company reported fourfold revenue growth over the past 12 months, with 90% of its revenue generated outside India. It has not disclosed its absolute revenue or valuation following the latest funding round.
Live2.ai plans to use the investment to expand its enterprise operations and develop its AI capabilities for customers in international markets.

candidates.snippet: Ex-Tencent AI researcher raises tens of millions in angel round for robot touch sensors Dealroom
candidates.text:
Fundraise Nov 4, 2026, 20:15 UTC
Ex-Tencent AI researcher raises tens of millions in angel round for robot touch sensors
What's the deal? Inspiration Robotics (AGIMind Robotics), a Chinese tactile intelligence startup, has raised tens of millions of yuan in an angel round from Leaguer Capital, Hefei Innovation Investment Dealroom has a profile for this one. Try Dealroom → , and other backers, with Zhizhen Consulting as financial adviser. The company builds vision-based tactile sensors that let robots sense force, slippage, and deformation to improve fine manipulation.
Who's behind it? Founder and chief executive officer Zhang Yazhan holds a robotics doctorate from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology and was a senior AI researcher at Tencent , where he led large-scale data pipelines and AI model development. He later worked as a researcher and doctoral supervisor at a national laboratory, focusing on tactile perception and fine-manipulation models.
What's the product? Its Lux-series vision-based tactile sensors have reached volume delivery across several fields, the company says. They use a self-developed "dense force field" approach that extracts force, deformation, slippage, and pose data from a single image, and their small size lets them fit robotic arms, grippers, and dexterous hands.
What's the money for? The round will fund production-line construction, mass-production capacity, and further development of its tactile intelligence systems. Beyond Lux, the company is exploring electronic skin, six-axis force sensors, and new tactile products, while expanding into data-collection systems and pipelines.
What's the endgame? Zhang says the long-term goal is to build the physical-interaction infrastructure — "Embodied AI Infra" — that embodied AI models need. His argument: for physical AI to work in the real world, models must understand gravity, friction, and deformation, which vision alone cannot capture.
What could go wrong? The company says Lux has reached scale, but public information gives no delivery volumes, customers, or revenue, leaving commercial traction unproven.
The signal: The round lands as tactile sensing heats up — industry reports count about US$426.3M raised across humanoid robot sensors in the first seven months of 2026, with rivals like Paxini securing large deals. Against those, this round is small; its significance is that tactile hardware is moving from research toward a race for mass production, not proof of a mature "tactile intelligence" market.
